title: How AirDrop works without internet

segments.text: Your iPhone can send a photo to the phone next to you, with no internet at all. So how?
Your phone sends out a tiny Bluetooth Low Energy signal that says: I'm here. Nearby Apple devices hear it.
But Bluetooth Low Energy is much too slow for big files.
Step two: Wi-Fi, without a router.
The two phones open a direct Wi-Fi link, just between each other. No network, no internet. That's where your photo travels.
Step three: before anything is sent, the phones create an encrypted connection.
So Bluetooth finds, and Wi-Fi delivers.
That's why AirDrop needs Wi-Fi turned on, even when you're not connected to any Wi-Fi network.

sources: https://support.apple.com/guide/security/sec2261183f4 (Apple Platform Security: AirDrop uses BLE for discovery, then peer-to-peer Wi-Fi without internet or access point, encrypted with TLS)
https://support.apple.com/HT204144 (Use AirDrop on iPhone: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must be on, devices within about 30 feet / 10 m)
